page_title: Cut token costs in half with Dosu

summary.name: Dosu
summary.one_liner: Dosu is a knowledge infrastructure service that captures what engineering teams and their coding agents learn and keeps docs, specs, and agent memory current with the code.
use_cases: keep repository documentation current as code changes
reduce token spend of coding agents
query open source tool docs through public spaces
sync docs from Notion, Confluence, or Coda
summary.what_it_does: Dosu monitors code changes after being installed on GitHub or GitLab and updates docs to keep them fresh. It captures learnings from agent sessions and turns them into shared, team-wide knowledge and reusable skills. Users can add it to Slack or MS Teams to ask for context or have it document something. Knowledge is stored as human-readable markdown, is described as OKF compatible, and can sync with GitHub, Confluence, Notion, and similar tools. A single shell command adds the Dosu MCP Server so coding agents can query the shared context.
notable: Shared knowledge cache so agents reuse context instead of re-exploring the codebase
Markdown-based, OKF-compatible knowledge that is syncable and not locked into a silo
Single shell command to add the Dosu MCP Server to a coding agent
Free tier for public repositories and access to Dosu Public Spaces
caveats: Free tier is described for public repositories; other tiers and prices are not stated on the page
The 50% token reduction and 2x iteration speed figures are vendor claims shown on the page, not independently verified
